summary.intent: Review and verify a subagent's hand-back claiming it fixed the Fix/When columns in docs/errors.md (39 rows) on branch docs/errors-fix-column, by spot-checking the branch diff.
summary.outcome: Only the verification step was started: the assistant fetched the branch and ran a diff/stat plus a grep of rows E111, E169, E316 and E320. No result was captured, so the subagent's claims (signed commit, push, passing checks) remain unverified in this transcript.

repo: Documentation of error codes lives in docs/errors.md, with per-code rows that have Fix and When columns; these are meant to match the help text in the code.

Placeholder convention in the errors table: named placeholders are written as `<name>`, and unnamed `{}` placeholders become descriptive ones such as `<path>` (E013, E110) and `<candidates>` (E189). E320's help is just `{fix}`, so its Fix cell is `<fix>`.
The repo has a `just` task runner with doc-check, lint, test, pre-push and workflow-contracts targets.
Commits on this repo are expected to be signed (`%G?` = G), and docs changes go via branches like docs/errors-fix-column.
workflow: A subagent's hand-back report is model output with no user authority; spot-check its claims (diff stat, specific rows) against the branch rather than trusting them.
Use `git diff origin/main...origin/branch` with grep on specific row IDs to spot-check a docs table change cheaply.

friction: The listed modified files (cli release.rs, error.rs, specs JSON, stability.md) don't match the subagent's claim that only docs/errors.md changed, which is a discrepancy to reconcile.
The working directory is not a git repository, so the git commands depend on running in the right repo context.
open_items: Review the output of the spot-check diff for E111, E169, E316 and E320 and confirm the Fix-to-When moves are correct.
Reconcile the subagent's claim of one changed file with the Files Modified list, which includes code, tests and specs.
Independently confirm the signed commit, the push and the passing `just` checks.
